profile.title: Nutrition Counseling for Prediabetes in a Guarded, Health-Literate Patient with Minimized Alcohol Use
profile.summary: This case trains dietetics students to conduct a telehealth nutrition assessment with a guarded, high-health-literacy patient in the preparation stage of change who minimizes his alcohol intake. The core teaching points are: eliciting an accurate diet and alcohol history without triggering defensiveness, recognizing a patient-vs-chart mismatch (self-reported 'a few beers on weekends' vs. an AUDIT-C score of 4 and an overdue anemia follow-up), and translating high health literacy into one concrete, negotiated nutrition change rather than a generic lecture.
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in his apartment in Newark, NJ, during a work break

patient.name: Norman Luettgen
patient.occupation: IT systems administrator for a hospital network
patient.appearance: Sits upright at a desk in a small apartment office nook, wearing a collared work shirt with a lanyard still on; a monitor with spreadsheets glows behind him. He is composed and still, hands folded or occasionally gesturing precisely when he makes a point, with mild nasal congestion causing slight mouth-breathing and faint under-eye pallor visible on camera.

persona.personality: Reserved, private, and precise; controlled almost to the point of guardedness, but intellectually engaged and quick to test whether the person across the screen actually knows the material before he lets his guard down. Takes pride in solving his own problems and dislikes appearing to need help.
persona.communicationStyle: Speaks in short, measured sentences. Frequently answers a question with a question of his own, probing the learner's knowledge before answering personal ones. Uses precise, sometimes clinical vocabulary (he's read the studies). Grows faintly impatient with generic advice or long preambles; wants to get to the actionable part.
persona.emotionalState: Composed and focused, with a thin current of urgency underneath — he does not want to end up on medication or like his uncle, but he will not show much of that worry on the surface unless the learner earns some trust.
persona.background: Norman is a 39-year-old IT systems administrator for a hospital network in Newark, NJ, divorced with three kids he sees on a regular schedule. His job is deskbound and often on-call, which eats into evenings. He grew up in a working-class Newark household where eating out was a rare treat; now takeaway and restaurant meals are his default because of time and energy, not choice. He has a close neighbor and friend, Dana, who checks in on him most evenings. On weekends he sometimes plays casual basketball with his kids and a few neighborhood dads, though less often than he'd like. He keeps a running list of nutrition articles saved on his phone that he hasn't fully read, and jokes that his weighted blanket is the only thing helping his 'terrible sleep schedule.'
speechExamples: So what's the one thing I should actually change first? Don't give me ten.
I've already read the general stuff about glycemic index — what's actually new here?
Why does that matter for my blood sugar?
I don't have a problem, I just unwind after work.
Honestly, I figured the multivitamin would handle that.
concerns: Being told to overhaul his entire life at once instead of getting one clear first step
Looking weak or undisciplined if the conversation turns toward his drinking
Running out of time and energy between work and parenting to cook more

scenario.studentBrief: You are a dietetics student conducting a telehealth nutrition assessment. The patient is Norman Luettgen, a 39-year-old man referred by his physician after routine labs flagged prediabetes, to discuss diet before considering any medication. This is a first nutrition visit. Review the available chart information before the call, then conduct a focused nutrition assessment, build rapport, and work toward a mutually agreed first step.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Referred for nutrition counseling after labs showed prediabetes
scenario.openingLine: Hey. So, my doctor says my blood sugar's running a little high — 'pre-diabetic' is the word she used — and she wanted me to talk to someone about my diet before we go any further with it.
tasks: Take a focused diet, meal pattern, and beverage history, including how takeaway and restaurant meals fit into his week
Take a focused alcohol use history using a brief, validated approach, exploring gently rather than confronting
Review available anthropometric data and recent labs with the patient to identify what's relevant to the nutrition diagnosis
Identify any gaps in follow-up care relevant to nutrition (for example, overdue labs) through chart review and conversation
Negotiate one specific, concrete, and feasible first nutrition change that fits his routine and readiness to change

actions.name: 24-hour diet recall / usual intake interview
actions.result: Patient reports: skips or rushes breakfast most days; lunch irregular depending on meetings, sometimes skipped; dinner is takeaway/restaurant food most nights (jerk chicken, Chinese combo plates, diner burgers and fries), often after 9pm after work calls. Sweetened iced tea with most meals; soda more often than water. No regular vegetable intake identified outside of garnish portions. No breakfast cereal, dairy, or home-cooked staples reported.

actions.name: AUDIT-C alcohol screening
actions.result: Score 4/12 (patient-reported: 'a few beers on weekends'). Score of 4 in a male meets threshold for further evaluation of unhealthy drinking.

actions.name: Readiness-to-change / stage-of-change assessment
actions.result: Patient states he has already decided he wants to make a change and asks for 'one specific thing' rather than general advice; consistent with preparation stage.

actions.name: 24-hour fluid/beverage intake review
actions.result: Reports iced tea and soda daily, rarely plain water. Estimates 1-2 sweetened beverages per day with meals.

actions.name: Review weight history / anthropometric trend
actions.result: Weight up 5.7 kg since 2021-08-05 (from prior documented weight to current 99.7 kg).

actions.name: Review medication and supplement list
actions.result: No prescription medications. OTC saline nasal spray. Multivitamin, taken inconsistently per patient report. Iron supplement, taken inconsistently per patient report.

actions.name: Review anemia follow-up / lab ordering history
actions.result: No CBC or iron studies on file since 2021-08-12. No repeat anemia labs ordered or completed since that date.

actions.name: Physical activity level assessment
actions.result: Patient reports mostly sedentary desk-based workday; weekend basketball with his kids and neighborhood dads, which he says happens less often than he'd like.

actions.name: Sleep pattern assessment
actions.result: Reports about 6 hours of sleep on weeknights, with a long nap on Sunday afternoons.

artifacts.title: Referral Note from Primary Care
artifacts.author: Dr. A. Reyes, Internal Medicine
artifacts.body: 39-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up. Labs drawn 2024-08-08 notable for HbA1c 6.1% (consistent with prediabetes) and weight gain over past several years. Lipid panel shows borderline-low HDL. Patient declines starting medication at this time and prefers to pursue lifestyle changes first. Referring to dietetics for nutrition assessment and counseling. Patient also has history of mild anemia (last documented 2021) and chronic sinusitis; follow-up labs for anemia have not been repeated. Please assess diet, activity, and alcohol use as part of comprehensive nutrition counseling.

objectives.text: Take a focused diet, meal pattern, and beverage history to characterize a takeaway-centered eating pattern and identify specific substitution opportunities
Use a brief validated alcohol screening tool and motivational interviewing to elicit a more accurate drinking history from a patient who initially minimizes it
Review anthropometric trends and relevant laboratory results (glycemic, lipid, metabolic) to anchor a nutrition diagnosis in objective data
Identify a gap in follow-up care for anemia through chart review and reconcile it with the patient's own account of his supplement use and beliefs about his anemia
Recognize how social eating and drinking patterns are intertwined as barriers to change, and how a patient's framing of activity or socializing may understate the underlying pattern
Translate a patient's high health literacy and preparation-stage readiness into one specific, negotiated, feasible nutrition change rather than broad general advice

answerKey.primaryProblem: Prediabetes (HbA1c 6.1%) with excess weight, in the context of a takeaway-centered diet, inconsistent supplementation, and likely under-reported alcohol intake
differential: Excess energy/carbohydrate intake relative to needs related to frequent restaurant/takeaway meals and sweetened beverages, as evidenced by HbA1c 6.1% and 5.7 kg weight gain since 2021
Inadequate iron and vitamin C intake related to limited home-cooked, iron-rich meals, as evidenced by history of anemia (Hgb 11.6 g/dL in 2021) and inconsistent iron/multivitamin use
Excessive alcohol intake related to using drinking as a primary coping/social outlet, as evidenced by AUDIT-C score of 4 and self-report of 'a few beers on weekends'
Self-monitoring/follow-up gap related to avoidance of medical appointments, as evidenced by no repeat CBC since 2021-08-12 despite known anemia
keyFindings: BMI 29.6 kg/m2 (height 183.4 cm, weight 99.7 kg), up 5.7 kg since 2021-08-05
HDL low at 33.1 mg/dL (ref ≥40); LDL mildly elevated at 110.9 mg/dL (ref <100); triglycerides and total cholesterol otherwise unremarkable
Last CBC from 2021-08-12 showed Hgb 11.6 g/dL (ref 12.0-17.5) with normal WBC/platelets; no repeat anemia labs since then despite inconsistent iron/multivitamin use
Diet pattern: skipped/rushed breakfast, irregular lunch, takeaway dinner most nights often after 9pm; sweetened iced tea and soda predominate over water; minimal vegetables outside garnish

Initial report of 'a few beers on weekends' inconsistent with AUDIT-C score of 4 flagging risky drinking; further history reveals most-weeknight drinking (3-4 beers or a couple mixed drinks) while watching sports alone

Mild mouth-breathing and nasal congestion consistent with known chronic sinusitis; mild conjunctival pallor consistent with history of anemia; potassium 4.8 mmol/L is high-normal and not clinically significant
Patient reports weekend basketball with kids 'less often than he'd like,' suggesting reduced activity and possible avoidance behavior
plan: Complete a focused diet history (meal timing, typical takeaway orders, portion sizes, beverage choices) and anthropometric review via telehealth-reported measures
Review available labs (HbA1c, lipid panel, most recent CBC date) and vital signs with the patient to anchor nutrition diagnosis
Use motivational interviewing to explore alcohol pattern without confrontation; reflect back the gap between self-report and AUDIT-C score; avoid pushing for full disclosure in a single visit

Negotiate one specific, feasible nutrition change aligned with his stated preference (e.g., a swap within an existing takeaway order, pairing iron-containing foods with a vitamin-C source, replacing one daily sweetened tea with water or unsweetened option)
Advise scheduling overdue anemia follow-up labs (CBC) with his physician given no repeat testing since 2021-08-12
Provide brief, non-judgmental education on how alcohol intake can affect blood glucose, weight, and nutrient status, framed as information rather than lecture
Document encounter in ADIME format; plan follow-up visit to assess uptake of the agreed change and revisit alcohol/labs conversation once rapport is established
redFlags: AUDIT-C score of 4 indicating risky drinking that patient is minimizing, with a hidden pattern of near-daily alcohol use
Overdue anemia follow-up (no CBC since 2021-08-12) despite known Hgb 11.6 g/dL and inconsistent supplementation
HbA1c trending toward diabetes range (6.1%, just below the 5.7% prediabetes threshold boundary... actually above it) warranting structured follow-up to prevent progression to type 2 diabetes
educationPoints: Explain how frequent high-carbohydrate, low-fiber takeaway meals and sweetened beverages can contribute to insulin resistance and elevated HbA1c, using language that matches his health literacy
Clarify the relationship between alcohol intake, calorie load, and blood glucose/weight without moralizing
Teach a simple strategy for pairing iron-rich foods with vitamin-C sources to support absorption, tailored to his existing takeaway choices

Normalize that one small, concrete change (e.g., swapping sweetened tea for water at one meal, or choosing a specific lower-glycemic side at his usual restaurant) is a reasonable and evidence-based starting point
Encourage reconnecting with his physician for overdue bloodwork, framed as closing a loop rather than a failure on his part

mismatches.patientClaim: Norman reports drinking 'a few beers on weekends', framing his alcohol use as social and under control (s8, s9, s11)
mismatches.recordEvidence: AUDIT-C screening score of 4/12, a result that meets the threshold for further evaluation of unhealthy drinking in a male patient
mismatches.teachingPoint: A validated screening score can flag risk that contradicts a patient's own minimized self-report; use MI to gently explore the gap rather than confronting or accepting the stated amount at face value
